rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadhf and damgh are metaphors from perceptible action, while haqq and batil are abstract; the shared relation makes the borrowing intelligible.
rows.anchor: فالقذف والدمغ مستعاران وهما محسوسان والحق والباطل مستعار لهما وهما معقولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tangible rope is borrowed to signify the abstract covenant.
rows.anchor: استعير الحبل المحسوس للعهد وهو معقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣadʿ, literally cracking glass, stands for conveying the message; its image stresses a certain, forceful effect, unlike mere conveying, which may fail to affect listeners.
rows.anchor: استعير الصدع وهو كسر الزجاجة وهو محسوس للتبليغ وهو معقول والجماع التأثير

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says humility can either lower or elevate a person; the wing image here means using humility that raises one before God.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب لما كان الذل على ضربين ضرب يضع الإنسان

words: ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The listed expressions borrow perceptible things for intelligible meanings, with an intellectual relation linking image and meaning.
rows.anchor: كلها من استعارة المحسوس للمعقول والجامع عقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In describing the water's excess, the abstract idea of arrogance is borrowed for perceptible abundance; the common feature is elevation.
rows.anchor: المستعار منه التكبر وهو عقلي والمستعار له كثرة الماء وهو حسي والجامع الاستعلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other examples borrow an abstract quality for perceptible things: Hell nearly splitting from rage and daylight made seeing.
rows.anchor: المستعار له كثرة الماء وهو حسي والجامع الاستعلاء وهو عقلي أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An original metaphor uses a borrowed generic noun, as in rope, darkness and light, or valley.
rows.anchor: أصلية وهي ما كان اللفظ المستعار فيها اسم جنس

words: فَٱلْتَقَطَهُۥٓ ءَالُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A derivative metaphor uses a non-generic form, including verbs and particles; here the lām is borrowed after comparing enmity and grief following the finding with an outcome implied by a goal.
rows.anchor: وتبعية وهي ما كان اللفظ فيها غير اسم جنس كالفعل والمشتقات

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd reports that the Qur'an was arranged from written fragments in the Prophet's presence.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت قال كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نؤلف القرآن من الرقاع

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi explains that this first gathering means arranging separately revealed verses into their sūras at the Prophet's direction.
rows.anchor: قال البيهقي يشبه أن يكون أن المراد به تأليف ما نزل من الآيات المتفرقة في سورها

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: After the battle of Yamama, Umar urged Abu Bakr to gather the Qur'an because deaths among reciters might cause much of it to be lost; Abu Bakr initially objected that the Prophet had not done so, then agreed.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو بكر إن عمر أتاني فقال إن القتل قد استحر بقراء القرآن

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Abu Bakr chose Zayd for his youth, intelligence, trustworthiness, and prior work writing revelation; Zayd gathered the Qur'an from palm stalks, stones, and people’s memories.
rows.anchor: قال زيد قال أبو بكر إنك شاب عاقل لا نتهمك

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd found the close of Sūrat al-Tawba with Abu Khuzayma alone; the sheets stayed with Abu Bakr, then Umar, then Hafsa.
rows.anchor: ووجدت آخر سورة التوبة مع أبي خزيمة الأنصاري لم أجدها مع غيره

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali called Abu Bakr the most rewarded person regarding the codices because he was the first to gather God's Book.
rows.anchor: عن عبد خير قال سمعت عليا يقول أعظم الناس في المصاحف أجرا أبو بكر

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin transmits Ali's account that after the Prophet died, Ali vowed to leave home only for Friday prayer until he had gathered the Qur'an, and then did so.
rows.anchor: من طريق ابن سيرين قال قال علي لما مات رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم آليت

words: فَمِنْهُم مَّنْ هَدَى ٱللَّهُ وَمِنْهُم مَّنْ حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a truly feminine subject, the feminine marker is usually retained; omission is possible when another word intervenes, and becomes more apt as the separation grows.
rows.anchor: الحقيقي لا تحذف تاء التأنيث من فعله غالبا إلا إن وقع فصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With non-natural feminine nouns, omission is preferable when there is separation, increasingly so with longer intervening material.
rows.anchor: وأما غير الحقيقي فالحذف فيه مع الفصل أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Affirming the feminine marker is also acceptable; Sūrat Hūd contains both marked and unmarked forms.
rows.anchor: فجمع بينهما في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians prefer omission because God placed the unmarked form before the marked form where both occur.
rows.anchor: وأشار بعضهم إلى ترجيح الحذف واستدل بأن الله قدمه على الإثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omission is also permitted without an intervening word when the subject is an explicit noun, but not when it is a pronoun.
rows.anchor: ويجوز الحذف أيضا مع عدم الفصل حيث الإسناد إلى ظاهره فإن كان إلى ضميره امتنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a pronoun or demonstrative separates mismatched masculine and feminine terms, it may agree in either gender; the examples follow the preceding masculine noun or predicate.
rows.anchor: جاز في الضمير والإشارة التذكير والتأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Generic nouns may be masculine by reference to the genus or feminine by reference to a collective; the passage also cites both readings of 'the cattle resemble one another' and parallel wind and sky forms.
rows.anchor: وكل أسماء الأجناس يجوز فيها التذكير حملا على الجنس والتأنيث حملا على الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms differ both because the second has more separating words, favoring omission, and because min refers to the feminine collective umma while fariq is masculine; Arabic may relax agreement when an equivalent expression lacks the marker.
rows.anchor: لوجهين لفظي وهو كثرة حروف الفاصل في الثاني والحذف مع كثرة الحواجز أكثر ومعنوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that stopping should follow the Uthmanic codex spelling in substitution, addition, deletion, joining, and separation, subject to transmitted exceptions in particular words.
rows.anchor: أجمعوا على لزوم اتباع رسم المصاحف العثمانية في الوقف إبدالا وإثباتا وحذفا ووصلا وقطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported stop-spelling exceptions include adding wāw in yadʿu al-insān, yawm yadʿu al-dāʿ, and sanadʿu al-zabāniya, alongside specific hā, yā, alif, and joining conventions.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويدع الإنسان ﴾ ﴿ يوم يدع الداع ﴾ ﴿ سندع الزبانية ﴾

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr pauses on ka'ayyin with yā and connects certain forms, while some other reciters follow the codex spelling throughout.
rows.anchor: فإن أبا عمرو يقف عليه بالياء ويوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kull denotes all individuals of an indefinite noun to which it is annexed, all members of a definite plural, or all parts of a definite singular.
rows.anchor: اسم موضوع لاستغراق أفراد المنكر المضاف هو إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kull can modify a noun to express completeness, emphasize a definite noun for totality, or follow an operator as a noun; its construction changes with each function.
rows.anchor: أحدها أن تكون نعتا لنكرة أو معرفة فتدل على كماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When kull is annexed to an indefinite, agreement in its pronoun must follow its meaning, as in 'every human'.
rows.anchor: وحيث أضيفت إلى منكر وجب في ضميرها مراعاة معناها نحو

words: إِن كُلُّ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّآ ءَاتِى ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَبْدًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When kull is annexed to a definite, its agreement can follow its singular masculine form or its collective meaning; both occur across this verse and the next clause.
rows.anchor: أو إلى معرف جاز مراعاة لفظها في الإفراد والتذكير ومراعاة معناها وقد اجتمعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same alternatives of agreement apply when kull stands without annexation, as the cited examples show.
rows.anchor: أو قطعت فكذلك نحو ﴿ قل كل يعمل على شاكلته ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a negative particle or verb governs kull, the negation is directed specifically at comprehensiveness.
rows.anchor: وحيث وقعت في حيز النفي بأن تقدمت عليها أداته أو الفعل المنفي فالنفي موجه إلى الشمول خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭā'irahu means his deed.
rows.anchor: ﴿ طائره ﴾ عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among forms written to agree with anomalous readings are variants for 'their omen' and 'his omen on his neck'; the list also includes a variant of 'enter among My servants'.
rows.anchor: ( إنما طئرهم ) ( طئره في عنقه )

words: وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُۥ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ كِتَٰبًۭا يَلْقَىٰهُ مَنشُورًا
rows.speaker: شمس الدين بن الصائغ
rows.claim: Shams al-Din ibn al-Sa'igh catalogs more than forty end-rhyme adjustments, including fronting objects, clauses, temporal phrases, and pronouns; deleting or adding final letters, altering declension, and masculinizing generic nouns.
rows.anchor: ألف الشيخ شمس الدين بن الصائغ كتابا سماه إحكام الراي في أحكام الآي قال فيه

words: وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُۥ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ كِتَٰبًۭا يَلْقَىٰهُ مَنشُورًا
rows.speaker: شمس الدين بن الصائغ
rows.claim: His list says this verse places a clausal modifier before a single-word modifier for the sake of the verse ending.
rows.anchor: الخامس تقديم الصفة الجملة على الصفة المفرد نحو

rows.speaker: شمس الدين بن الصائغ
rows.claim: Other rhyme adjustments he lists include putting the governed word before its governor, putting a later event first, prioritizing the lesser item, and fronting a pronoun before its referent.
rows.anchor: أحدها تقديم المعمول إما على العامل نحو

rows.speaker: شمس الدين بن الصائغ
rows.claim: He also lists deleting final yā from a definite adjective, an unjussived verb, and an annexed pronoun, and adding long vowels or retaining them with a jussive.
rows.anchor: السادس حذف ياء المنقوص المعرف نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taf'taʾ means 'you continue' or 'you do not cease'.
rows.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ تفتأ ﴾ قال لا تزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khashyat imlāq means fear of poverty.
rows.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ خشية إملاق ﴾ قال مخافة الفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥadāʾiq means gardens.
rows.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ حدائق ﴾ قال البساتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word muqīt means powerful and fully capable; al-Aḥyaḥ al-Anṣārī's verse uses it for one able to restrain himself from harming an enemy.
rows.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ مقيتا ﴾ قال قادرا مقتدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā yaʾūduhu means 'does not burden Him'.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا يؤوده ﴾ قال لا يثقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sariyyā means a small stream.
rows.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ سريا ﴾ قال النهر الصغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaʾsan dihāqan means a full cup.
rows.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ وكأسا دهاقا ﴾ قال ملأى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains kanūd as ungrateful for blessings: a person who eats alone, withholds his help, and starves his servant; a cited poem uses the word for ingratitude.
rows.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ لكنود ﴾ قال كفور للنعم وهو الذي يأكل وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasayunghiḍūna means they shake their heads in mockery.
rows.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ فسينغضون إليك رؤوسهم ﴾ قال يحركون رؤوسهم استهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuhraʿūn means they come rushing toward him in anger.
rows.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ يهرعون ﴾ قال يقبلون إليه بالغضب

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
rows.claim: The Prophet told Ibn Salam that the sun and moon had once been two suns; the dark mark on the moon is the erasure of its sign, referring to God's effacing the night sign.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد المقبري أن عبد الله بن سلام سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن السواد الذي في القمر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Jabir has the Prophet explain human honor as eating with one's fingers.
rows.anchor: قال ( الكرامة الأكل بالأصابع )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says each people is summoned with its leader and the Book of its Lord.
rows.anchor: قال يدعى كل قوم بإمام لهم وكتاب ربهم )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Umar has the Prophet explain the sun's dُلūk as its decline from the zenith; a second report from Ibn Umar gives the same explanation but has a weak chain.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ﴿ أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس ﴾ قال ( لزوال الشمس )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi authenticates, and al-Nasa'i transmits, the Prophet's explanation that angels of night and day witness the dawn recitation.
rows.anchor: قال ( تشهد ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet explains the Praiseworthy Station as the intercession for his community; another wording says simply 'the intercession', and the report has many routes in canonical collections.
rows.anchor: قال ( هو المقام الذي أشفع فيه لأمتي )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a report from Anas, the Prophet answers that the One who made people walk on their feet can make them walk on their faces when gathered.
rows.anchor: قال ( الذي أمشاهم على أرجلهم قادر أن يمشيهم على وجوههم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is a preposition, subjunctive particle, jussive particle, or non-governing particle; the preposition is usually kasra with an overt noun and fatha with a pronoun, apart from yāʾ.
rows.anchor: أربعة أقسام جارة وناصبة وجازمة ومهملة غير عاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām may mark entitlement or a relation between a meaning and its possessor, as in praise belonging to God and woe belonging to the defrauders.
rows.anchor: الاستحقاق وهي الواقعة بين معنى وذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lām can indicate a particular relationship or attachment, as in someone having a father or siblings.
rows.anchor: والاختصاص نحو ﴿ إن له أبا ﴾ ﴿ فإن كان له إخوة ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lām can indicate ownership, as in God's possession of what is in the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: والملك نحو ﴿ له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām may be causative: the verse means that because of his love of wealth, a person is intensely miserly.
rows.anchor: والتعليل نحو ﴿ وإنه لحب الخير لشديد ﴾ أي وإنه من أجل حب المال لبخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Hamza's reading of the covenant verse, lām is causative: God took the covenant because He had given the prophets scripture and wisdom, and so that they would believe in the later messenger.
rows.anchor: في قراءة حمزة أي لأجل إيتائي إياكم بعض الكتاب والحكمة ثم لمجيء محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the lām in li-īlāf Quraysh, some attach it to 'let them worship' and others to the preceding clause; the latter is preferred because Ubayy's codex joined the two as one sūra.
rows.anchor: وتعلقها ب يعبدوا وقيل بما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In some expressions lām carries the sense of ilā, 'toward' or 'until'.
rows.anchor: وموافقة إلى نحو ﴿ بأن ربك أوحى لها ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lām can carry the sense of ʿalā, 'on' or 'against', as in falling on chins, lying on one's side, and the curse being upon people.
rows.anchor: وعلى نحو ﴿ ويخرون للأذقان ﴾ ﴿ دعانا لجنبه ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lām can mean 'in' for the Day of Resurrection or its appointed time; 'for my life' may mean during my life or, alternatively, for the sake of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي في حياتي وقيل هي فيها للتعليل أي لأجل حياتي في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lām can mean 'about' or 'concerning': the unbelievers speak about the believers, rather than addressing them directly, as shown by the expected wording of their reproach.
rows.anchor: أي عنهم وفي حقهم لا أنهم خاطبوا به المؤمنين وإلا لقيل ما سبقتمونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 'for the sun's dُلūk', lām may carry the sense 'after'.
rows.anchor: وبعد نحو ﴿ أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this metaphor class one side is literal and the other figurative: fire's 'calling' is figurative, and Hell as the mother of sinners is a refuge and return like a human mother sheltering her child.
rows.anchor: فإن الدعاء من النار مجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linguistic metaphor uses a word outside its original assignment; one type names the whole for a part, such as 'fingers' for fingertips or 'bodies' for faces.
rows.anchor: الثالث إطلاق إسم الكل على الجزء نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the witnessed month the whole month uses the whole for a part; al-Fakhr al-Razi explains that the command means whoever sees its beginning must fast all of it, even if later traveling.
rows.anchor: أطلق الشهر وهو إسم لثلاثين ليلة وأراد جزء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reverse figure names a part for the whole: 'face' means God's essence or the person facing, body-wide states are expressed by faces or hands, and prayer's standing, reciting, bowing, or prostrating can stand for the whole prayer.
rows.anchor: عبر بالوجوه عن جميع الأجساد لأن التنعم والنصب حاصل بكلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 'a sacrificial offering reaching the Kaaba', the Kaaba names the whole sanctuary, since the offering is not slaughtered inside the building itself.
rows.anchor: أي الحرم كله بدليل أنه لا يذبح فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some count the seven oft-repeated verses as a Medinan exception in Sūrat al-Ḥijr.
rows.anchor: استثنى بعضهم منها ﴿ ولقد آتيناك سبعا ﴾ الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti says the verse about those who precede and those who lag behind should also be excepted, based on reports that it was revealed about rows in prayer.
rows.anchor: لما أخرجه الترمذي وغيره في سبب نزولها وأنها في صفوف الصلاة

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi reports that all of Sūrat al-Naḥl is Meccan except its closing verses beginning 'if you retaliate'.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أبو الشيخ عن الشعبي قال نزلت النحل كلها بمكة إلا هؤلاء الآيات

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the passage from 'those who emigrated for God' to the end of al-Naḥl is Medinan and the preceding passage is Meccan; the account from Jabir ibn Zayd divides it as forty Meccan verses and the rest Medinan, while a report about 16:90 is cited against this.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عن قتادة قال سورة النحل من قوله ﴿ والذين هاجروا في الله من بعد ما ظلموا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra's cited Medinan exceptions include the Spirit question, the passage about the unbelievers nearly tempting the Prophet, the challenge to bring a similar Qur'an, the vision, and 'those given knowledge before it'.
rows.anchor: الإسراء استثني منها ﴿ ويسألونك عن الروح ﴾ الآية لما أخرج البخاري عن ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The listed exceptions in al-Kahf are its opening through 'barren ground', the command to keep patient company, and 'those who believe' through the sūra's end.
rows.anchor: الكهف استثني من أولها إلى ﴿ جرزا ﴾ وقوله ﴿ واصبر نفسك ﴾ الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported exceptions in Maryam are the prostration verse and 'there is none of you but he will come to it'.
rows.anchor: مريم استثني منها آية السجدة وقوله ﴿ وإن منكم إلا واردها ﴾

words: وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزْوَٰجًۭا مِّنْهُمْ
rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti argues for another Medinan exception in Ta-Ha: Abu Rafiʿ reports that a Jewish lender demanded collateral for a loan of flour, after which the Prophet said he was trustworthy in heaven and earth and the verse forbidding coveting worldly provision was revealed.
rows.anchor: أخرج البزار وأبو يعلى عن أبي رافع قال أضاف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيفا فأرسلني إلى رجل من اليهود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A weak al-Awfi-chain report from Ibn Abbas says Thaqif asked the Prophet for a year before converting, and he considered granting it; the report would place the relevant revelation in Medina.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه من طريق العوفي عن ابن عباس أن ثقيفا قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أجلنا سنة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: A stronger report points to Mecca; its chain is hasan and a corroborating report from Saʿid ibn Jubayr raises it to ṣaḥīḥ, which al-Suyuti adopts.
rows.anchor: والأول يقتضي نزولها بمكة وإسناده حسن وله شاهد عند أبي الشيخ عن سعيد بن جبير يرتقي إلى درجة الصحيح

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: When two sound occasion reports conflict, al-Suyuti prefers the one whose transmitter witnessed the event. Ibn Masud's Bukhari account places the Spirit question in Medina among Jews, outweighing Ibn Abbas's report that Quraysh asked Jews for a question and implies Mecca; Bukhari's report is also stronger.
rows.anchor: وقد رجح بأن ما رواه البخاري أصح من غيره وبأن ابن مسعود كان حاضر القصة

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: When two occasion reports could both have happened close together, they can both explain the revelation: Hilal ibn Umayya's accusation and Uwaymir's question about finding a man with one's wife are reconciled as simultaneous occasions; al-Nawawi inclines to this, as did al-Khatib.
rows.anchor: جمع بينهما بأن أول ما وقع له ذلك هلال وصادف مجيء عويمر أيضا فنزلت في شأنهما معا

words: وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلرُّوحِ قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A question may be left without a fully specified answer when the questioner seeks only to provoke, as with the answer about the Spirit being from God's command.
rows.anchor: قد يعدل عن الجواب أصلا إذا كان السائل قصده التعنت

rows.speaker: صاحب الإفصاح
rows.claim: The Jews meant to confound the Prophet because rūḥ can denote the human soul, Qur'an, Jesus, Gabriel, another angel, or a class of angels; the deliberately general answer defeated their trap since any specific sense could be rejected.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب الإفصاح إنما سأل اليهود تعجيزا وتغليظا إذ كان الروح يقال بالاشتراك على روح الإنسان والقرآن وعيسى

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says an information-seeking question may take its second object directly or with ʿan, more often with ʿan, as in the Spirit question.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب السؤال إذا كان للتعريف تعدى إلى المفعول الثاني

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: For asking someone to provide a thing, the verb may take the object directly or with min, more often directly; the examples concern asking for goods, reimbursement, and God's bounty.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان لاستدعاء مال فإنه يعدى بنفسه أو بمن وبنفسه أكثر
